problem_statement: When an AUX flash slot is configured in the build, the flashpage MTD driver makes `mtd_aux` available as a `mtd_dev_t *` that behaves like an ordinary MTD device. A caller that initializes `mtd_aux` and then performs raw page writes, aligned page writes, reads, and sector erases gets the written data back, including writes that cross page and sector boundaries and overwrites of an existing region. The reported page size, pages per sector, and sector count are consistent with the underlying flashpage geometry.

verification.reason: The statement describes the behaviour of mtd_aux well but omits the three names the build/test configuration relies on: the feature periph_flashpage_aux, the Make variable SLOT_AUX_LEN, and the C macro CONFIG_SLOT_AUX_LEN. These are public interface names that can be added to the statement without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The test Makefile sets FEATURES_OPTIONAL += periph_flashpage_aux and the test code is guarded by #ifdef MODULE_PERIPH_FLASHPAGE_AUX. The statement never names the feature 'periph_flashpage_aux', so the agent cannot register it in the build system or make the preprocessor guard work.

The test Makefile sets SLOT_AUX_LEN := 0x8000 to configure the AUX slot. The statement says 'when an AUX flash slot is configured in the build' but never gives the name of the Make variable, so the agent cannot wire the build system to the C code.

The fix translates SLOT_AUX_LEN into the C macro CONFIG_SLOT_AUX_LEN (via -DCONFIG_SLOT_AUX_LEN=$(SLOT_AUX_LEN)) and guards the mtd_aux definition with #if CONFIG_SLOT_AUX_LEN. The statement never names this C macro, so the agent cannot connect the Make variable to the C code.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrase about the build system defining CONFIG_SLOT_AUX_LEN and CONFIG_SLOT_AUX_OFFSET when SLOT_AUX_LEN is non-zero hints at the Makefile implementation from the fix, but it is not a major leak because the essential public interface (feature name, build variable, module guard, mtd_aux behavior) is needed by the tests.
leak_check.suggested_statement: When the `periph_flashpage_aux` feature is enabled in the build and the auxiliary slot is configured via the build variable `SLOT_AUX_LEN` (size of the aux slot in bytes) to a non-zero value, the flashpage MTD driver makes `mtd_aux` available as a `mtd_dev_t *` that behaves like an ordinary MTD device. The module guard `MODULE_PERIPH_FLASHPAGE_AUX` must be defined in such configurations so that code can conditionally use `mtd_aux`. A caller that initializes `mtd_aux` and then performs raw page writes, aligned page writes, reads, and sector erases gets the written data back, including writes that cross page and sector boundaries and overwrites of an existing region. The reported page size, pages per sector, and sector count are consistent with the underlying flashpage geometry.
